stories.title: Iya, the Camp-Eater
stories.text: Iya came to a camp disguised as a baby, and from inside the camp he swallowed it. A young mother noticed the strange sounds the baby made, and the people slipped away at midnight. At dawn Iya chased them, but his thin legs could not carry his great body, and warriors with long knives brought him down. The whole camp walked out of him, free.

stories.title: Old Double-Face
stories.credit: From Zitkala-Ša, Old Indian Legends (1901), and Charles Eastman (Ohiyesa) with Elaine Goodale Eastman, Wigwam Evenings. DRAFT text.
stories.text: Old Double-Face was a giant with a face in front and a face behind, so no one could creep up on him. He lured children away from the camps. Once he carried off a baby boy and kept him far from his people. Manstin the rabbit hid behind a sage bush and shot him through the heart. The boy was free, and he grew up to be a young man.
